description: Acute bacterial disease caused by Bacillus anthracis, often associated with contaminated soil after heavy rains or excavation. Can cause sudden death with minimal warning. A zoonotic disease: never open a carcass or handle blood without protection.
symptoms: swelling of neck brisket or flanks
bloated carcass appearance if found dead
critical_symptoms: swelling of neck brisket or flanks
first_aid: Do not open, bleed, or butcher any dead animal when anthrax is suspected.
Isolate live sick animals and keep people and other animals away from the area.
Mark and protect the site; avoid disturbing soil where animals graze or died.
Notify government veterinary services immediately for carcass disposal and diagnosis.
Vaccinate unaffected animals only under official veterinary direction after confirmation.
